extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society / 17th-century natural philosophers and experimental scientists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and reporting observational and experimental natural philosophy communications: recording measurements, methods, illustrations, analyses, and comparisons so fellow scientists can evaluate and reproduce the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct pendulum clock times by observed altitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: "the times of the pendulum clock being corrected by observed altitudes"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibrate chronometric timing with astronomical altitude observations before reporting timed events (used here when timing occultations). Include the correction method and corrected times in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive apparent planetary diameters from occultation durations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the known lunar diameter and the measured duration of an occultation to compute the apparent diameter of the occulted planet (example: "the whole duration of this occultation being known... it presently becomes known... that the diameter of Jupiter comes out 30' 53''").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the input values (lunar diameter, measured interval between limb contacts) and show the calculation linking timing to apparent angular diameter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple instruments to cross-check observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare observations made with different telescopes (example: observations made with a 20-foot telescope and with one of 3 feet "as well with a telescope of 20 feet as with one of 3").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results from distinct instruments and note agreement or discrepancies to support reliability of measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record detailed observational logs (times, contacts, altitudes, heights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a precise sequence of observational events with times and altitudes (examples: moon rose at X, sun rose at Y, Jupiter touched limb at time Z, heights measured at particular instants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full event chronology, local times, altitudes/heights, and any adjustments made (e.g. clock corrections) so others can reproduce or re-evaluate observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Botanical illustrations: as large and as natural as possible, include parts and microscope views
rubrics_metrics.description: "the figures will be as large as one leaf of the noble French paper will admit. If the plant be too large, it will be represented in pieces, all, or some at least, of the natural size, with their seeds, flowers, &c. and some parts and small plants as they appear in the microscope."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate plants at life-size when possible; for large specimens, show them in pieces and include seeds, flowers, and microscopic detail so morphological features are unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide trials and methods to ascertain soil nature
rubrics_metrics.description: "promises a trial of several means to ascertain the nature of soils, the causes of their particular disposition to certain plants, &c."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe and document multiple experimental approaches to determining soil properties and their effects on plant distribution, including procedures and comparative results.

rubrics_metrics.name: List products obtained by fire-decomposition and treat changes as alterations
rubrics_metrics.description: When subjecting plant material to heat, enumerate the products (example list: "1. Acid spirits. 2. Essential oils. 3. Sulphureous spirit. 4. Simple waters... 14. Earth") and treat these results as alterations by fire rather than separations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the classes of material obtained under controlled combustion, specifying how products were distinguished and the limitations of interpreting them as constituent separations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record experimental particulars: time, degrees of fire, sensible qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: "the particulars of the process are remarked and registered, as the time, degrees of fire, sensible qualities of the parts, &c."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document procedural parameters (timing, temperature/degree of heat, observable changes) for each experiment; use thermometry where possible and record units/methods for measuring heat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use thermometer and compare heat sources (culinary, stomachal, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: "several ways have been thought of, as, the manner of process, ascertaining the degrees of heat by a thermometer, &c. That culinary heat, and the heat of the stomach may make the same alterations and separations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report temperatures with a thermometer and, where relevant, compare effects of different heat sources to assess equivalence of treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect quantitative data with care, exactness, and judgment (weights, gravities)
rubrics_metrics.description: "these according to their proportionable quantities and degrees, and that with great care, exactness, and judgment, collected from different ways of examination: taking an account of their weight, gravity..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include precise quantitative measurements (mass, specific gravity, proportions) and describe measurement methods and uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use chemical indicators and simple qualitative tests to distinguish substances
rubrics_metrics.description: "Insensible qualities, found by divers mixtures; as, of acids, sulphurs, &c. with turnsole. Volatile spirits, &c. make solution of sublimate white. Sea-salt whitens solution of sacharum saturni. Mixed spirits redden solution of vitriol, &c."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ and report straightforward chemical tests/indicators (litmus/turnsole, reactions with salts and solutions) to characterize extracts and components, giving observed colour or reaction outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try extracts in vacuo to detect contained 'airs' and distinguish volatile vs fixed salts
rubrics_metrics.description: "Next the trying of these extracts in vacuo is propounded to find their air. And several observations of the differences of volatile and fixed salts related."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform vacuum experiments on extracts to observe released gases/volatile components and describe procedures and observations that distinguish volatile from fixed residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine degrees of composition and tailor methods for particular plants
rubrics_metrics.description: "And several observations... ways are shown how to find the degrees of composition of these extracts: particular ways for particular plants."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe analytical methods used to estimate proportions/composition and indicate when and how methods are adapted for different plant materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe methods for analyzing juices and state their advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: "Lastly, the way of analysing juices is mentioned; and the advantages of this process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the procedure for juice analysis and explicitly state the analytical benefits and limitations of the chosen technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standardized symbolic notation and label data/problem elements
rubrics_metrics.description: "Their capitals stand for the logarithms of the number signified by the small letters. D signifies data, or given; Q quaestitum, Prob. problem. Res. resolution."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define symbols and conventions at the start of mathematical problems; label given data (D), the sought quantity (Q), and present the resolution (Res.) to make reasoning and calculations transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify mathematical problems into ranks and present symbolic solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are "distinguished into three ranks" (first rank: compound interest for a single sum; second: annuities in arrear; third: annuities anticipated) with symbolic statements for D, Q, Res.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group problems by type/rank and use consistent symbolic formulas for each class so readers can apply rules to analogous cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish reproducibility by repeating trials across days and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: "After many trials repeated several days one after another, and with various ways of examination, still in every one of them with the same success..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate reproducibility by performing repeated trials over multiple days and with varied examination methods; report consistency and any divergences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report experimental setup, cycle counts and failure modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: sealed glass in a spherical receiver "after about 200 exhaustions had been made, it broke all in pieces in the receiver with a very great noise, by the elasticity of the air inclosed in the glass globe."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe apparatus and operating cycles (e.g. number of exhaustions), and report observed failure modes, so others can judge durability and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise anatomical descriptions, enumerate features, and correct prior errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed enumeration of anatomical facts about the torpedo (e.g., pores/glands, brain position, heart auricle count, ovarium/oviducts, benumbing muscles) and pointing out prior misstatements ("Dr. Willis has mistaken penultim for ultim").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give systematic anatomical descriptions, note functional inferences, and explicitly compare with or correct previously published accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe geological/cavern features with measured dimensions and observed biota
rubrics_metrics.description: Cavern account includes entrance location, vertical drops, roof heights, widths, lengths (e.g., "roof... about 8 fathoms... extends in length about 200 yards"), streams, sand beds, bats and aquatic life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report site measurements (depth, height, width, length), notable physical features, presence of flora/fauna, and any materials of practical use (e.g., sand for casting), to enable spatial and ecological assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require accurate, well-engraved illustrations after the author's exact delineations
rubrics_metrics.description: "These are so illustrated by figures well graven after the author's own exact delineations, that there is hardly any room left for addition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality engravings based on the author's precise drawings to accompany descriptive text so visual details are reliably communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe preparation, handling, and observable properties of novel materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of Kunckel's "pills" and phosphorus: preparation, how to handle (moisten/scrape) and observable effects (yield a considerable light, smoke; produce light in water when shaken).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting new materials or preparations, state preparation method, handling instructions, and reproducible observable properties (including demonstration conditions) so others can test claims.
